fields.Front: What are the core functional requirements to clarify for an Amazon Locker OOD interview?
fields.Back: 1) A courier drops a package into a locker sized to fit it. 2) The system generates a pickup access code and notifies the recipient. 3) The recipient enters the code to unlock and retrieve the package. 4) Unclaimed packages expire after a pickup window. 5) A single locker bank has a fixed, mixed set of locker sizes to allocate efficiently.

fields.Front: What should you explicitly mark out of scope when designing an Amazon Locker system in an interview?
fields.Back: Physical hardware/lock mechanism details, courier route optimization, and payment/billing — focus on locker allocation, access-code lifecycle, and the size-assignment strategy.

fields.Front: What is the responsibility of the LockerBank class?
fields.Back: Represents one physical location: owns a fixed set of Lockers of mixed sizes, and exposes assignLocker(Package) / releaseLocker(code) as the entry points for courier drop-off and customer pickup.

fields.Front: What is the responsibility of the Locker class?
fields.Back: One physical compartment: tracks its own LockerSize, LockerStatus, the Package currently inside (if any), and the current access code plus its expiration; exposes unlock(code).

fields.Front: What is the responsibility of the Package class?
fields.Back: Holds the tracking id, recipient info, and the LockerSize the package requires — it is a passive data object with no knowledge of which locker it ends up in.

Composition: a LockerBank owns a fixed collection of Lockers (typically a mix of sizes decided at install time); lockers don't exist outside a bank and are looked up by the bank when allocating or releasing.

fields.Front: Which design pattern fits locker-size assignment, and why?
fields.Back: Strategy. A LockerSizeAssignmentStrategy interface (e.g. BestFitStrategy, FirstAvailableStrategy) lets LockerBank swap the allocation algorithm — best-fit to minimize wasted space vs. first-available for speed — without changing the bank's calling code.

fields.Front: What is the shape of LockerBank.assignLocker()'s API and return value?
fields.Back: assignLocker(Package pkg) filters lockers to AVAILABLE ones whose size is ≥ the package's required size, delegates the final pick to the assignment strategy, marks that locker OCCUPIED, generates an access code, and returns both the locker and the code.

fields.Front: What must Locker.unlock(code) check, in order, before releasing the package?
fields.Back: 1) The locker is actually OCCUPIED (not already empty). 2) The access code hasn't expired (raise/return an expiry-specific error, not a generic failure). 3) The entered code matches. Only then does it release the package and reset status to AVAILABLE.

fields.Front: Edge case: no locker of the exact required size is available at drop-off time. What should the assignment strategy do?
fields.Back: Fall back to the next size up (never a smaller one, or the package won't physically fit) — e.g. a BestFit strategy that finds no MEDIUM locker free should consider LARGE next, and only raise a NoLockerAvailableException if every size ≥ required is full.

fields.Front: Edge case: a recipient never enters their access code within the pickup window (e.g. 3 days). What should happen?
fields.Back: The system auto-expires the code, marks the package for return-to-sender/carrier pickup, notifies the recipient and sender, and frees the locker back to AVAILABLE once the carrier physically retrieves the package (status can pass through a transient RESERVED/pending-return state, not straight to AVAILABLE while the package is still inside).

fields.Front: Edge case: two couriers could simultaneously try to drop packages into the same locker bank at the exact same time. How does the design prevent a double-assignment?
fields.Back: assignLocker() must perform an atomic check-and-set on a locker's status (e.g. compare-and-swap AVAILABLE→OCCUPIED under a lock/transaction) rather than read-then-write, so two concurrent calls can never both succeed in claiming the same Locker.

fields.Front: Edge case: a recipient forgets/loses their access code. What recovery path should the design support?
fields.Back: Expose a regenerateAccessCode(package) flow gated by identity verification (e.g. re-authenticating in the retailer's app) that invalidates the old code and issues a new one with a fresh expiration, without changing the locker's contents or status.

public interface LockerSizeAssignmentStrategy {
    Locker selectLocker(Package pkg, List<Locker> availableLockers);
}

public class BestFitStrategy implements LockerSizeAssignmentStrategy {
    @Override
    public Locker selectLocker(Package pkg, List<Locker> availableLockers) {
        return availableLockers.stream()
            .filter(locker -> locker.getSize().ordinal() >= pkg.getRequiredSize().ordinal())
            .filter(locker -> locker.getStatus() == LockerStatus.AVAILABLE)
            .min(Comparator.comparing(locker -> locker.getSize().ordinal()))
            .orElseThrow(() -> new NoLockerAvailableException(pkg.getId()));
    }
}

import random
import string

class LockerBank:
    def __init__(self, lockers, strategy):
        self.lockers = lockers
        self.strategy = strategy

    def assign_locker(self, package):
        available = [l for l in self.lockers if l.status == LockerStatus.AVAILABLE]
        locker = self.strategy.select_locker(package, available)
        code = self._generate_access_code()
        locker.status = LockerStatus.OCCUPIED
        locker.package = package
        locker.access_code = code
        return locker, code

    def _generate_access_code(self):
        return "".join(random.choices(string.digits, k=6))

public class Locker {
    private LockerStatus status;
    private String accessCode;
    private LocalDateTime codeExpiresAt;
    private Package contents;

    public boolean unlock(String enteredCode) {
        if (status != LockerStatus.OCCUPIED) {
            return false;
        }
        if (LocalDateTime.now().isAfter(codeExpiresAt)) {
            throw new AccessCodeExpiredException();
        }
        if (!accessCode.equals(enteredCode)) {
            return false;
        }
        status = LockerStatus.AVAILABLE;
        contents = null;
        accessCode = null;
        return true;
    }
}

fields.Front: (Python) Implement a fallback strategy that widens to the next larger size when the primary strategy finds nothing.
fields.Back:
class FirstAvailableFallbackStrategy(LockerSizeAssignmentStrategy):
    def __init__(self, primary_strategy):
        self.primary_strategy = primary_strategy

    def select_locker(self, package, available_lockers):
        try:
            return self.primary_strategy.select_locker(package, available_lockers)
        except NoLockerAvailableError:
            largest = max(available_lockers, key=lambda l: l.size.value, default=None)
            if largest is None:
                raise
            return largest

fields.Text: The core classes in an Amazon Locker design are {{c1::LockerBank}} (a physical location), {{c2::Locker}} (one compartment), {{c3::Package}}, and {{c4::LockerSizeAssignmentStrategy}} (chooses which locker fits a package).
The LockerSize enum is ordered {{c1::SMALL}}, {{c2::MEDIUM}}, {{c3::LARGE}}, {{c4::EXTRA_LARGE}} so sizes can be compared to find the smallest locker that still fits a package.
The LockerStatus enum for a single compartment is {{c1::AVAILABLE}}, {{c2::OCCUPIED}}, {{c3::RESERVED}}, and {{c4::OUT_OF_SERVICE}}.
